messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: P1 detected -> customer: SableBridge (enterprise/vpc)
incident-bot: symptom = auth failures on ingress (401-ish), ~85% requests failing for tenant=sablebridge, started 2023-11-12T01:49Z. Runbook: https://go/runbooks/vpc-auth-issues :rotating_light:
pagerduty: Paging oncall: @maria.s (primary)

maria.s: Acked. Oncall here, looking.

alex.m: Any immediate customer impact? is traffic still flowing at all or just auth failures?

sablebridge-sre: Confirming from SableBridge: users see "auth failed" and some services 503 downstream, majority of requests rejected at our auth layer. They can still reach the token endpoint on idp.sablebridge.example.

samir.k: I'm seeing these in the auth-service logs (filtered):
```
2023-11-12T01:48:52Z auth-verify error="token validation failed" tenant=sablebridge err="issuer mismatch: got 'https://idp.old.example', expected 'https://idp.sablebridge.example'"
2023-11-12T01:49:10Z mtls error="handshake failed" remote_ip=10.2.4.5 err="x509: certificate has expired"
```

maria.s: So two things? issuer claim mismatch AND mTLS handshake errors. Samir, can you confirm whether the jwks fetch is returning new keys or old keys?

samir.k: Doing fetch from discovery on our side (cached):
```
curl -s https://idp.sablebridge.example/.well-known/openid-configuration | jq '.issuer, .jwks_uri'
"https://idp.sablebridge.example"
"https://idp.sablebridge.example/.well-known/jwks.json"
```
But when fetching jwks we still see the old kid set (keys A,B) while the tokens presented have kid=C. Looks like their signing key rotated but the jwks endpoint is lagging or metadata mismatch.

jin.lee: We cache OIDC discovery for 5m by default and have a separate cache for jwks with 10m TTL. Could be metadata stale, but token kid mismatch implies provider didn't publish new jwks. Also mtls error suggests their client cert chain used for mutual TLS (they upload certs for tenant) is expired.

katie.p: SableBridge says they pushed a new signing key and rotated their IDP earlier this morning. They also ran cert renewals but a script may have failed to upload the intermediate cert to our tenant profile.

sablebridge-sre: Confirmed: we rotated signing keys at 01:40Z. JWKS endpoint is currently returning old keys due to CDN caching in front of our idp. Also our rotation script didn't attach the intermediate cert to the mTLS client bundle; we can upload immediately if you can accept our new chain.

maria.s: Ok. Immediate mitigations: 1) Invalidate our OIDC discovery/jwks caches for tenant sablebridge. 2) Temporarily allow a secondary issuer mapping for that tenant (issuer alias) so tokens with the updated iss pass validation. 3) For mTLS, allow a temporary bypass to accept client cert chains that present the new chain (short lived). We'll coordinate with product/eng-platform for safe flags.

alex.m: I can invalidate cache now and trigger an immediate jwks refetch for tenant=sablebridge.

alex.m: (running) `curl -X PURGE https://auth-cache.internal/tenants/sablebridge/jwks` -> response 200

samir.k: Refetching jwks: result shows new kid C present now. Token validation should accept tokens with kid C after refetch. However we still see some mTLS fails.

ops-runner: mTLS failure sample:
```
Nov 12 01:50:03 auth-proxy mtls: handshake error from 10.2.4.5: tls: failed to verify client certificate: x509: certificate has expired
```

jin.lee: That error is from our side verifying the client cert presented by SableBridge. If their uploaded client chain is missing the new intermediate, verification will fail. We can short-term relax verification for the tenant by adding the leaf cert as trusted (not ideal, but buys time). Need eng-platform approval.

katie.p: SableBridge can push the full chain in ~5-10m. They asked if we can keep flows running for their important traffic until they finish.

maria.s: Proposed plan:
- Step A (immediate): Invalidate OIDC/jwks cache + refetch (done).
- Step B (5-10m): Accept alternative issuer mapping for tokens (enable tenant alias) to tolerate iss mismatch during rotation window.
- Step C (10-30m): Coordinate with SableBridge to upload full mTLS chain; temporarily add leaf cert to tenant trust store if upload delayed.
- Step D (post-remediation): Roll back relaxations, verify rotation, run regression tests, and schedule postmortem.

alex.m: I've enabled a temporary issuer alias for tenant=sablebridge pointing to https://idp.sablebridge.example-alt for 15m. Flag: `tenant.auth.issuer_alias.sablebridge=enabled` (will auto-expire). Monitoring now.

samir.k: After jwks refetch and alias enable, error rate dropped from 85% -> 12% over last 6 minutes. Majority of remaining errors are mtls cert verification.

sablebridge-sre: Upload of full chain started, reporting CDN purge in progress too. ETA ~7m.

ops-runner: To speed, if they give us the PEM we can manually append intermediate into the tenant cert bundle: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" --data-binary @chain.pem https://api.redwood.internal/tenants/sablebridge/certs` — but we need SRE approval.

maria.s: Approve manual upload if customer can't complete in time. @samir.k can you be ready to revert this once they finish? Also record audit event.

samir.k: Will do. Uploading now on standby.

(7 minutes pass)

sablebridge-sre: Done — full chain uploaded and CDN purge finished. Customer reports success for a subset of users.

samir.k: I can see successful mtls handshakes in proxy logs now:
```
Nov 12 01:57:21 auth-proxy mtls: handshake ok tenant=sablebridge peer="CN=sablebridge-client"
```
Error rate now down to ~1.5% (background retries/tokens issued before rotation window).

maria.s: Great. Actions now: cancel issuer alias after 10 more minutes to ensure no regressions, run traffic holdback check, then revert any temporary trust-store changes if we took them.

katie.p: Customer impact summary for support: majority of requests were rejected for ~18 minutes, some downstream 503s, no credential leakage, root cause = simultaneous key rotation + CDN caching + incomplete mTLS chain upload on customer side.

sablebridge-sre: Confirmed. We'll add a check in our rotation script to invalidate CDN edge cache and include full chain. Sorry for the hit.

maria.s: Post-incident follow-ups: 
- Add auto-cache-invalidation to our OIDC refetch path when discovery changes.
- Consider reducing jwks cache TTL for enterprise tenants with dedicated pools.
- Add monitoring alert for mtls client cert expiry 7d/1d/1h before expiration.
- Schedule joint runbook review with SableBridge ops next week.

alex.m: Logging incident as INC-2023-11012-SABLEBRIDGE. I'll hand off to oncall shadow for postmortem and close after RCA.

maria.s: Thanks team. Marking resolved in pagerduty. If anyone sees regression, re-open thread.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged -> marked RESOLVED by maria.s (oncall) at 2023-11-12T02:03Z :white_check_mark:

ops-runner: Adding final note: temporary issuer alias was disabled at 2023-11-12T02:13Z, jwks cache behavior adjusted for tenant, and mtls expiry alert rule pushed to prod monitoring.

maria.s: Closing thread. Postmortem assignment: alex.m (author), samir.k (infra), jin.lee (platform), katie.p (customer comms).
